notes: Extracted unchanged except: the three anonymous rules are named rule:comp-*; odrl:conflict odrl:prohibit is made explicit (it equals the DPROD profile default). Classified odrl-core: the policy names the DPROD profile, as the original does, but uses only operand-binding vocabulary, which is not a profile term (conformance README). Obligations. Both duties are root obligations; each states no target, so each receives the policy-level target employee-compensation (normalisation spec §6.2), and with no assignee anywhere the bearer is the request subject (due2-profiles.md §6). Both constraints read request-source operands (ex:retentionPeriod, odrl:purpose), so they are guards read against the request (due2-workflows.md v0.4 §5.2) — DPROD's activation reading (D-ACTIVATE): rule:comp-anonymization is owed when the request's purpose is analytics, as the comment intends, and rule:comp-retention-limit when the request states a retention period over P7Y. Each is in force when rule:comp-hr-division-read matches the request, constraints aside, and its guard holds; a missing operand makes the guard U and the status unknown (§6.1). No scenario has delete or anonymize evidence, so an obligation in force is outstanding. DPROD never collects either duty for a read, because step 1 collects a duty only when its own action matches the request (exception 6 of §8.2). Neither duty has a deadline, so neither can be violated. Scenario 6 is added to show the retention guard holding. DPROD Σ assumed in every scenario: Σ₀ with clock = request.at, performed = ∅; no duty is collected, so Σ' = Σ. Scenarios 3 and 4 are DPROD Failures that due2 decides or reports Indeterminate: and(error, false) is false in Kleene logic but Failure under DPROD's left-to-right short-circuit (§6.1). Swapping the two conjuncts of the authored odrl:and would turn DPROD's scenario 3 into NotApplicable, which is the order-sensitivity gap of §8.2. These are refinements, not exceptions. Scenario 5 shows DPROD masking the same error structurally, because NormActive checks the subject before the condition.

Permit. The permission matches. rule:comp-anonymization's guard (purpose eq analytics) is F, so it is not in force; rule:comp-retention-limit's guard reads ex:retentionPeriod, which the request does not state, so it is U and the obligation unknown.

analytics ∉ {compliance, operations}, so the permission is F: NotApplicable. It still matches, constraints aside. rule:comp-anonymization's guard reads this request's purpose, analytics, so it is in force; with no anonymize evidence it is outstanding. The retention guard is U (no retention period), so that obligation is unknown.

The purpose atom is U (missing) and the legal-basis atom F; U ∧ F = F, so the permission is F whatever the purpose. NotApplicable. The permission matches; both guards read missing request values (purpose, retention period), so both obligations are unknown.

T ∧ U = U, so the permission is U. The permissive completion gives Permit, the restrictive one NotApplicable. The permission matches: the anonymization guard is F (compliance), so it is not in force; the retention guard is U, so that obligation is unknown. Neither has a deadline, and an obligation never changes the verdict (§6.1).
